translations.answer: The original steps to verify are: print asset.joint_names or asset_cfg.joint_names in the training environment, and align it with the legged-gym, real machine SDK, and deployment endpoint observation/action arrays. There may be DFS/BFS order differences between Isaac Gym/legged-gym and Isaac Sim/Orbit; if the strategy includes a height scan, XY/YX order must be verified in Isaac Sim/Orbit. The author confirmed that the motor order between legged-gym and Orbit is different, but did not report only the corrected order in real machine results, so this is a mandatory interface check, not an isolated fix.
translations.applicability: This applies to transferring strategies from legged-gym/Isaac Gym to Isaac Sim/Orbit or real GO1. The specific order must be based on the target version's printed results.
translations.credibility.rationale: The environment, processing steps, and results have engineering records, but formal cross-verification or independent replication is lacking.
translations.details.attempts.0: The maintainer provided code to print the joint order and explained the DFS/BFS order difference with height scan.
translations.details.attempts.1: The author replaced the actuator net with a PD model and retrained.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: Print asset.joint_names or asset_cfg.joint_names in the training environment and align it with the real machine SDK, legged-gym, and deployment endpoint observation/action arrays.
translations.details.diagnostics.1: If using a height scan, verify XY/YX order in Isaac Sim/Orbit.
translations.details.diagnostics.2: Perform A/B testing of joint order correction and actuator model replacement separately to avoid conflating multiple changes.
translations.details.effective_fixes.0: In the specific environment, the author replaced the actuator model and retrained, resulting in no kicking or shaking of the legs and power protection in real GO1 at zero velocity commands.
translations.details.environments.0: Orbit/Isaac Lab unitree-go1-flat policy (2024-04), real Unitree GO1, ONNX Runtime C++, original post did not provide precise submission, SDK, or firmware version.
translations.details.limits.0: Cannot assert all GO1 actuator nets are faulty from this thread.
translations.details.limits.1: No information on PD stiffness/damping, action limits, strategy submission, or real machine SDK version provided.
translations.details.limits.2: Height scan is a maintenance hint, and the original author did not report whether it participated in the strategy.
translations.details.outcomes.0: The real machine symptoms are resolved; however, joint order correction and actuator model replacement were not isolated, and the root cause remains unclosed.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: When the Unitree GO1 strategy is online after boot, it should first verify which interface is causing the leg kicking and power protection.
translations.details.safety_notes.0: Involves real machine leg kicking and power protection; re-initialization must use a crane or safety rope, low gain, action and torque limits, emergency stop, and personnel isolation.
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: The author confirmed that the motor order between legged-gym and Orbit is different.
translations.details.suspected_causes.1: The author suspects the GO1 actuator net, but the thread does not prove it is the only root cause.
translations.details.symptoms.0: At zero velocity commands, the real GO1 legs kick, shake, and enter power protection.
